Question: A can do a piece of work in 17 days and B in 13 days. How long will they take working together?
Explanation:
Method 1: LCM / Total Work (Recommended)
• Assume total work is the LCM of 17 and 13, which is 221 units.
• A's efficiency = 221 ÷ 17 = 13 units/day.
• B's efficiency = 221 ÷ 13 = 17 units/day.
• Combined efficiency = 13 + 17 = 30 units/day.
• Total time = 221 units ÷ 30 units/day = 7.37 days.

Method 2: Direct Formula
• Total Time = (a × b) / (a + b) = (17 × 13) / (17 + 13) = 7.37 days.

Method 1: LCM / Total Work (Recommended)
• Assume total work is the LCM of 53 and 12, which is 636 units.
• A's efficiency = 636 ÷ 53 = 12 units/day.
• B's efficiency = 636 ÷ 12 = 53 units/day.
• Combined efficiency = 12 + 53 = 65 units/day.
• Total time = 636 units ÷ 65 units/day = 9.78 days.

Method 2: Direct Formula
• Total Time = (a × b) / (a + b) = (53 × 12) / (53 + 12) = 9.78 days.
